amendments.rule: Gapping is not a new case. When a parallel line omits its verb, the copula the ASV supplies joins the predicate that licenses it, exactly as in rule 20, and is never `added`. **But that covers the copula and nothing more, exactly as rule 20's own boundary does.** Where the line's missing verb is a lexical one and the ASV writes a lexical verb for it, no morpheme in that line is there to carry the word, and it is its own `added` unit under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause: `כִּי־מַפְרִיס פַּרְסָה הוּא וְלֹא גֵרָה` → *because he parteth the hoof but* ***cheweth*** *not the cud* gives *but* to the waw under rule 14, *not* to the negative, and *the cud* to the noun with its supplied *the* under rule 15, leaving the supplied *cheweth* `added`. Do not read *omits its verb* above as a licence to fold such a word into the negative, the connective or the noun standing beside it, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. Test by subtraction as rules 16, 31 and 43 do — drop the English verb and ask whether a morpheme standing in that line has lost its rendering, or whether what has gone is a predication the Hebrew never wrote there. **But read whether the Hebrew writes that verb anywhere in the coordination before counting.** Where a verb the Hebrew writes once is realized twice across coordinated clauses, both occurrences are that verb's one possibly discontinuous unit under rule 25, exactly as a distributed `מִן` takes both of its *from*s there; what the preceding sentences govern is a line whose verb the Hebrew leaves unwritten altogether.
amendments.why: DEU.14.8 met the case rule 34 had not considered: the ASV supplies a whole lexical verb for a gapped line (`וְלֹא גֵרָה` → *but cheweth not the cud*), and rule 34 as written says of a parallel line that omits its verb that the supplied word is *never added*. Rule 20 already draws the boundary for a clause with no verb in it at all, so the correction is a narrowing of rule 34 rather than new doctrine — but leaving rule 34's sentence unqualified is what lets a later pass fold such a verb into the negative or the noun beside it. The example, the subtraction test and the rule 25 rider are all drawn from rules already in the contract, and no corpus row shown for this chapter's lemmas bears against it.

conventions: Two-word English animal and bird names in this chapter's clean-and-unclean lists are headed by rule 31's tie-break, not by its subtraction test alone. Where the second word is a class noun the ASV also writes for another Hebrew word of that class, the modifier is the ASV's specifier and the head stays on the class noun: *wild goat* (v.5) on *goat*, which v.4 writes alone for `עֵז`; *gier eagle* (v.12) on *eagle*, written alone for `נֶשֶׁר` in the same verse; *night hawk* (v.15) on *hawk*, written alone for `נֵץ` in the same verse; and *little owl*, *great owl*, *horned owl* (v.16) all on *owl*, which no verse writes bare but which stands as the class noun across three coordinate members for three distinct Hebrew words, on the JOB.4.10-11 lion pattern. Where the second word is instead a generic the ASV would write for anything, the head is the modifier: *abominable thing* (v.3) on *abominable*, *creeping things* (v.19) on *creeping*, *strong drink* (v.26) on *strong*. *sea mew* (v.15) heads on *mew* by the plain subtraction test, *sea* being the specifier on a word that already names the bird. Heading each of the three owls on its modifier was the live alternative and is named in v.16's note; the chapter took the class-noun reading uniformly.

report: Checked all 32 candidate lemma groups and, because the table is blind to them, the five `added` units read against every parallel clause in the chapter. Every difference the table flags is one the ASV or the morphology licenses, so patches is empty.

The possessive lamed + suffix group is the one that looks like a split and is not. vv.9-10 leave the resumptive suffix `unrepresented` because the fused kol + asher rendered *whatsoever* supplies the English subject; vv.27, 29 give the suffix *he* because no relative stands in those clauses. Rule 43's closing sentence divides them on exactly those terms, and all four units keep the negation word on `אַיִן` and the *hath* on `לְ`.

Supplied prepositions are consistent across the two rules that claim them: vv.11, 20, 21, 26 put the word on the verb because the Hebrew object is bare (rule 44), while v.22 puts *from* on `הַשָּׂדֶה` because that noun is an adverbial accusative (rule 33). That is rule 44's own stated limit, not a divergence.

The three supplied object pronouns *it* (vv.21, 25, 28) are `added` uniformly, and the one supplied coordinator (v.6, the italic *and* before *cheweth*) is `added` because that clause is asyndetic. Counted the chapter's waws and its `אוֹ` against the ASV's connectives verse by verse; no surplus on either side anywhere else.

Head choices on two-word animal and bird names follow rule 31's two branches consistently — the class noun where the ASV writes that noun for another Hebrew word of the class (*goat*, *eagle*, *hawk*, *owl*), the modifier where the second word is a generic (*thing*, *things*, *drink*), and *mew* in *sea mew* by plain subtraction. Recorded as a convention below.

BSB: all 17 disagreements are documented convention differences — rule 40 recastings that leave `בְּ`/`לְ` nothing (vv.2, 8, 25), rules 29/47 articles (vv.2, 7, 19, 23, 28), rule 16 object markers (vv.7, 8), rule 22 resumptives (vv.10, 12, 25) and the cognate `שֶׁסַע` (v.6), the unrendered `הוּא` of v.19, and rule 32 on the paragogic `Sh` he of `רָחָמָה` (v.17). None is a genuine error and none was changed.

The one contract gap this chapter met is rule 34's gapping sentence against v.8's supplied lexical *cheweth*. Amended rule 34 rather than adding a rule: rule 20 already draws the boundary, and it is rule 34's own wording — *when a parallel line omits its verb ... is never added* — that invites the wrong reading, so the correction belongs where that sentence stands.

Not promoted: the class-noun head reading behind the v.16 owls. Generalising it would contradict rule 31's own `עֹלָה` → *burnt offerings* example, which has the same coordinate shape (*burnt*, *sin*, *meal* offering) and is settled the other way. A chapter convention carries it without putting a self-contradicting rule into the contract.

The four `כֹּל אֲשֶׁר` → *whatsoever* fusions (vv.9, 10, 26 twice) are all headed on `כֹּל`. Rule 23 settles that on both of its tests — `כֹּל` carries quantification the relative lacks, and it also stands first and governs — so the verse notes' hedge is conservative and no convention is needed.
